subject: Post-demo privacy Qs — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach timing (action items)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@medsynchealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo privacy Qs — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach timing (action items)

Hi Alicia + Tom,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great conversation. Per promise, I'm consolidating the privacy/DPA follow-ups we discussed so your legal/compliance team can review. Attached is our standard DPA (DPA_Redwood_v2.pdf) and the public subprocessor list.

Quick recap of the items you raised and the questions we need to confirm:
- Role: You indicated MedSync intends to remain the controller and Redwood will act as processor. We want to confirm that position and align on standard processor commitments.
- Subprocessors: Please confirm whether you require prior approval for new subprocessors or if a 30-day notice + objection window is sufficient. We can provide a running list and a notification cadence.
- Breach notices: You mentioned a tight notify window for incidents affecting PHI. What is your required first-notice SLA (e.g., 24h/48h)? We typically provide an initial notification within 48 hours with a follow-up detailed report.
- Data residency: You asked about keeping data in US regions only (no cross-border). We can enforce US-only residency for your tenant — want to confirm if that needs to be restricted to specific regions (us-east-1, us-west-2) or any US region is fine.
- Retention & logs: Clarify retention expectations for user data vs system logs. Typical patterns: redaction/ephemeral KV caching, logs retained 90 days by default; we can extend or provide export options.
- Evidence: We can share SOC2 type II report and encryption architecture docs (attached SOC2_report_2026.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm controller/processor posture (one-line)
2) Alicia/Tom to send any DPA redlines (you mentioned you'd share those) — I'll route to legal and get back within 48 business hours.
3) If agreeable, schedule a 30-minute legal sync early next week to run through redlines.

Attachments: DPA_Redwood_v2.pdf (pdf), subprocessor-list.csv (csv), SOC2_report_2026.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if it's easier.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127

From: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@medsynchealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medsynchealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy Qs — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach timing (action items)

Connor,

Thanks — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side (we're looped in Legal/Compliance internally):
- Controller/Processor: Yes — MedSync is the controller. Redwood will be a processor. We need the DPA to reflect processor obligations, including assistance with data subject requests.
- Subprocessors: We prefer prior written notice + 14-day objection window for any subprocessors that will process PHI. If a subprocessor is critical (infrastructure partners like AWS), a notice-only model is OK, but for any new analytics/embedding/third-party ML vendors we want prior approval.
- Breach notice: For incidents affecting PHI we require initial notification within 24 hours of detection and an updated remediation report within 72 hours.
- Residency: US-only is required, specifically restricted to us-east-1 and us-west-2.
- Retention: Patient records are subject to 7 year retention elsewhere in our contract; from Redwood as a processor, we expect no retention beyond processing unless explicitly agreed. System logs: 1 year required with secure export on request.
- Evidence: Please share SOC2 and typical encryption-at-rest/in-transit controls (we saw SOC2 doc, thanks).

We attached a quick DPA redline (MedSync_DPA_redlines.docx) with inline comments. Can you route to your legal and get back with proposed edits? We can do a legal sync on Tuesday morning.

Quick note: Tom (CC) is our Head of Engineering and will be on the sync if needed.

Thanks,
Alicia
Director of Product Partnerships | MedSync Health
alicia.grant@medsynchealth.com
[Attachment: MedSync_DPA_redlines.docx]
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T13:40:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo privacy Qs — routing to legal (MedSync redlines attached)

Laura / Marissa / Neha,

Forwarding Alicia's redlines and asks (attached). Key asks to respond to:
- Customer expects Redwood to be processor; they want DSAR assistance clause and processor obligations clarified.
- Subprocessor policy: they want prior written approval for any subprocessor touching PHI (14-day objection), notice-only acceptable for core infra.
- Breach notify: 24h initial, 72h detailed.
- Residency: restrict to us-east-1 & us-west-2 only for this tenant.
- Retention: no processor retention beyond processing; system logs retained 1 year.

Can you advise: 1) whether we can accept 14-day objection for PHI-touching subprocessors, or propose alternative language (e.g., notice + expedited objection and carveouts for infra), 2) whether we can commit to 24h initial notice for PHI incidents or stick with standard 48h, and 3) confirm operational feasibility for region restriction and 1-year log retention export capability.

Attachments: MedSync_DPA_redlines.docx

Connor

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T15:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo privacy Qs — routing to legal (MedSync redlines attached)

Connor, Marissa — pulled this together quickly for your reply to MedSync. Summary and recommended positions below; I can join the sync Tuesday if helpful.

Recommended positions (short):
- Role: Accept processor status. Add explicit DSAR assistance clause (we will timely provide exported data and cooperation per law).
- Subprocessors: Counter-propose notice + 14-day objection limited to non-infrastructure subprocessors that will have access to unredacted PHI. For core infra (IaaS/CDN) we remain notice-only. This balances security with operational agility.
- Breach notice: We can offer an initial notification within 48 hours and an expedited update within 72 hours. If MedSync insists on 24 hours for initial notice, we should confirm detection/triage timing — 48 hours is our operational baseline. Offer commitment to escalate if detection is confirmed sooner.
- Residency: We can commit to US-only residency. For strict region constraints (us-east-1 & us-west-2) ops needs a tenant flag; Marissa, can you confirm that the tenant deployment can be pinned to those regions?
- Retention/logs: Agree to restrict processor retention to only what's necessary for processing. Offer system logs retention set to 1 year with secure export on request; we can add an option in the contract to export logs monthly.
- Evidence: Provide SOC2 report (attached) and an export link to our subprocessor list; maintain a 30-day advance notice on subprocessor changes for non-PHI-touching partners and a narrower objection window per above.

Next steps to communicate to MedSync:
1) Confirm we accept processor role and will add DSAR support language.
2) Provide updated DPA with: proposed subprocessor language, breach notice language (48h initial / 72h detailed), residency pin, and retention/log export language.
3) Share SOC2 and live subprocessor link.
4) Offer a 30-minute legal/ops sync Tuesday 10:00am PT to walk redlines.

I'll draft the DPA edits now and upload a draft for Connor to send.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
